The files of a snapshot

Source: R/files.R
lake_files.Rd

lake_files() lists the snapshot's live files, one row per add action in force, with their partition values, statistics and deletion vector descriptors. lake_partitions() gives the distinct partition values of those files. lake_removed() lists the tombstones (remove actions) still in the log. lake_count() counts the snapshot's rows from the log alone.

Usage

lake_files(tbl, filter = NULL, stats = TRUE, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_partitions(tbl, filter = NULL, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_removed(tbl, int64 = c("double", "integer64"))

lake_count(tbl)

Arguments

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open().

filter

An expression over column names; see Details. NULL, the default, keeps every file.

stats

Whether to parse the files' statistics into num_records, null_count, min and max.

int64

How 64-bit integers from the log are returned: "double" (the default), exact up to 2^53 - 1 and an error of class zulake_error_int64 beyond it, or "integer64", from the bit64 package, exact from -2^63 + 1 to 2^63 - 1 (bit64 keeps -2^63 for NA, so that value is an error too). It applies to the columns that hold 64-bit counts and values; inside an action or commitInfo as the log writes it, only a number a double cannot hold becomes an integer64.

Value

lake_files() returns a data frame with one row per live file, sorted by path: path (as the log writes it, relative to the table or absolute), uri (where the file is), size_bytes, modification_time (POSIXct), data_change, partition (a list column of named lists of typed values), deletion_vector (a list column: the descriptor, or NULL), then, with stats = TRUE, num_records, null_count, min and max, and last action, the add action as the log holds it.

lake_partitions() returns a data frame with one column per partition column and one row per distinct combination of values among the live files the filter keeps; a table without partition columns has none.

lake_removed() returns a data frame with one row per tombstone: path, deletion_timestamp (POSIXct), data_change, size_bytes, partition_values (a list column of the values as the log writes them), deletion_vector and action.

lake_count() returns the number of rows, a double: the sum of numRecords over the live files minus the rows their deletion vectors delete (each descriptor's cardinality). When a live file has no numRecords the count is unknown: NA_real_, with a warning of class zulake_warning_count_unknown whose files field gives the number of such files. It is never a partial sum. A file with a deletion vector and no numRecords breaks the protocol: zulake_error_corrupt_log.

Details

Partition values are typed by the column's Delta type: byte and short as integers, integer as doubles (an R integer cannot hold -2^31), long as 64-bit values (see int64), float and double as doubles, boolean as logicals, date as Date, timestamp and timestamp_ntz as POSIXct in UTC, and decimal, string and binary as the text the log holds. A null partition value is NA.

Statistics come from each file's stats JSON, keyed by column name: min and max typed as partition values are, except that a decimal statistic stays its JSON text exactly as the log writes it, since a double would round it; null_count and num_records are 64-bit counts. Statistics are optional in the protocol, so a file can have none (NA and NULL).

filter is an unevaluated R expression over column names, of comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=), %in% and is.na() joined by !, & and |, with literals or values from the calling environment. A file is kept when the filter can be TRUE for it: on a partition column the filter is evaluated exactly, as R evaluates it, on the file's partition values; a comparison on any other column cannot rule a file out yet, so it keeps every file. Any other call is refused with a zulake_error_filter error, since there are no rows here to apply it to.

See also

lake_summary() for the totals in one row, lake_changes() for the files added and removed between two versions.

Examples

# A partitioned table of two files, written by hand.
path <- tempfile("table")
dir.create(file.path(path, "_delta_log"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  '{"protocol":{"minReaderVersion":1,"minWriterVersion":2}}',
  paste0(
    '{"metaData":{"id":"example","format":{"provider":"parquet","options":{}},',
    '"schemaString":"{\\"type\\":\\"struct\\",\\"fields\\":[',
    '{\\"name\\":\\"id\\",\\"type\\":\\"long\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}},',
    '{\\"name\\":\\"year\\",\\"type\\":\\"integer\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}}]}",',
    '"partitionColumns":["year"],"configuration":{}}}'
  ),
  paste0(
    '{"add":{"path":"year=2025/part-0.parquet","partitionValues":{"year":"2025"},',
    '"size":100,"modificationTime":0,"dataChange":true,',
    '"stats":"{\\"numRecords\\":3,\\"minValues\\":{\\"id\\":1},\\"maxValues\\":{\\"id\\":3}}"}}'
  ),
  paste0(
    '{"add":{"path":"year=2026/part-0.parquet","partitionValues":{"year":"2026"},',
    '"size":100,"modificationTime":0,"dataChange":true,',
    '"stats":"{\\"numRecords\\":2,\\"minValues\\":{\\"id\\":4},\\"maxValues\\":{\\"id\\":5}}"}}'
  )
), file.path(path, "_delta_log", "00000000000000000000.json"))

tbl <- lake_open(path)
lake_files(tbl)[c("path", "size_bytes", "num_records")]
#>                       path size_bytes num_records
#> 1 year=2025/part-0.parquet        100           3
#> 2 year=2026/part-0.parquet        100           2
lake_files(tbl, filter = year >= 2026)$path
#> [1] "year=2026/part-0.parquet"
lake_partitions(tbl)
#>   year
#> 1 2025
#> 2 2026
lake_count(tbl)
#> [1] 5
lake_removed(tbl)
#> [1] path               deletion_timestamp data_change        size_bytes        
#> [5] partition_values   deletion_vector    action            
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
